extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (postdocs, early-career researchers, junior professors and established academics) seeking individual research funding from the DFG
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and eligibility/aims for the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) individual grants programmes, covering research grants, fellowships, career programmes, clinical-trial funding, and related strategic instruments. Intended to guide potential applicants about which DFG programme fits their career stage, project type, and mobility/eligibility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility for individual grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers who have completed their academic training (as a rule, those who hold a doctorate) are eligible to submit project proposals with a defined thematic focus and project duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across the DFG individual grants programmes: typically aimed at researchers who have completed academic training (usually a doctorate) and proposing projects with clearly defined topics and durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Research grants enable individuals who have completed their academic training to conduct at any time research projects with clearly defined topics and durations, regardless of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-call, investigator-initiated funding for individual research projects; can be applied for at any time and across all subjects, provided the applicant has completed academic training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific networks offer early career researchers the opportunity to engage in scientific exchange and cooperation on topics of common interest across locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to foster collaboration and exchange among early career researchers across institutions/locations on shared topics; suitable for network-building and cooperative activities rather than single-investigator projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Fellowships are intended to help early career researchers to conduct a defined project at a location of their choice in a country other than Germany and to use it as an opportunity to familiarise themselves with new research methods or to bring a large project to a conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobility-focused funding for early-career researchers to work abroad; aimed at method acquisition, project completion, or international collaboration; eligibility targeted at early-career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emmy Noether Programme
rubrics_metrics.description: The Emmy Noether Programme gives exceptionally qualified early career researchers the chance to qualify for the post of professor at a university by leading an independent junior research group for a period of six years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target group: exceptionally qualified postdocs and junior professors with temporary contracts at an early career stage. Objective: lead an independent junior research group for up to six years to accelerate qualification for a professorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emmy Noether — applicant eligibility note
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme is open to postdocs and junior professors with temporary contracts who are at an early stage in their research careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies eligible career stages (postdoctoral researchers and junior professors on temporary contracts) for the Emmy Noether Programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heisenberg Programme
rubrics_metrics.description: If you already meet all the requirements for appointment to a permanent professorship, you can apply to the Heisenberg Programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides funding to enable applicants to continue high-quality research at an institution of their choice while preparing for a senior academic role and building their academic reputation; targeted at researchers who already fulfil professorship appointment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinhart Koselleck Projects
rubrics_metrics.description: This programme enables outstanding researchers with a proven scientific track record to pursue exceptionally innovative, higher-risk projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted funding for established, outstanding researchers to undertake high-risk/high-reward, exceptionally innovative research that may not fit conventional funding schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials Programme
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clinical Trials Programme enables individuals who have completed their academic training to conduct at any time patient-oriented clinical research within a temporary project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds interventional clinical studies, including feasibility studies (phase II) and interventional trials (phase III). Also funds observational trials provided the study investigates a highly relevant research question that cannot demonstrably be answered using an interventional design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshops for Early Career Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops for early career investigators are a strategic funding instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aimed particularly at established researchers who want to address a perceived lack of early-career researchers in their field by organising workshops for early-career investigators on specific topics; intended as a strategic measure to strengthen pipeline and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Academies
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of project academies is to enable professors from universities of applied sciences to engage in research projects based on DFG third-party funding at an early stage in their careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically targets professors at universities of applied sciences to involve them in DFG-funded research projects early in their careers, supporting research capacity-building in that institutional sector.
